outcomes.original: Filing step: File the DPH plan check application for the limited kitchen and bar layout with SF Department of Public Health, concurrent with or immediately after filing the ABC application. What to say: Submit scaled drawings of the kitchen, bar, hand sinks, restrooms, finishes, equipment list, and menu. Show the three-compartment sink, hand sinks at the bar and food prep areas, hot water supply, sealed surfaces, and mechanical ventilation. Include the food safety manager certificate. Schedule a pre-final inspection at 80% complete and a final pre-opening inspection at least two weeks in advance. Budget 21–60 days for plan review and 14–45 days for the permit to operate after the final inspection.

outcomes.original: Filing step: File the building permit application for tenant improvements with SF Department of Building Inspection, routed to Planning for zoning review, concurrent with the DPH plan check. What to say: Submit stamped plans for the bar build-out, kitchen hood and suppression system (if installing a new hood), ADA restroom upgrades, and any structural or mechanical work. Identify the project as tenant improvements with no change of use (bar to bar) and no change of occupancy. Include the DPH plan check approval as part of the routing. Coordinate electrical, plumbing, and mechanical permits with licensed subcontractors. Budget 14–120 days depending on the scope of work and whether Planning review is required.

outcomes.original: Filing step: If the limited kitchen uses grease (cooking oil, butter, or animal fat), register with SF Public Utilities Commission for the Fats, Oils & Grease program and install a grease interceptor before the final building inspection. What to say: Submit the Installation Verification Form to SFPUC after the interceptor is installed, sized per the Discharger Category assigned by the inspector. Budget 14–45 days for SFPUC review. outcomes.original: Filing step: Before opening, ensure all staff complete California Food Handler cards and RBS alcohol server training, subscribe to ASCAP and BMI music licenses, and register with EDD as an employer. What to say: Every employee handling food must obtain a Food Handler card within 30 days of hire (online, 2 hours, $7–15). Every employee serving alcohol must complete RBS training within 60 days of hire ($3 registration plus $10–25 course). Subscribe to ASCAP and BMI public performance licenses for recorded music ($300–2,500 each annually). Register with EDD for payroll taxes within 15 days of the first payroll. These are quick but often forgotten.

outcomes.original: Estimated time: 120 to 300 days. Estimated government cost: $5,900 to $21,200. Notes: The timeline and cost ranges cover a Conditional Use Authorization (120–300 days, $3,100–15,000 per the catalog entry for sf.conditional_use_authorization), health permit to operate (14–45 days, $470–1,000 per catalog:sf.health_permit), health plan check (21–60 days, $828–2,500 per catalog:sf.health_plan_check), and building permit (14–120 days, $800–15,000 per catalog:sf.building_permit). These are times to approval when the approvals are granted, measured from filing to decision; they do not include time to a denial or withdrawal. The ranges assume the CUA, health plan check, and building permit are filed concurrently or in close sequence, so the overall timeline is dominated by the CUA (the longest single approval). ABC license timelines and fees are not included because the alcohol type and license-acquisition strategy are not known. If the concept is confirmed to be a continuation of the prior bar use without a CUA, the timeline drops to 35–165 days and the cost to $2,800–6,200 (health and building only). The figures are from the permit catalog entries cited and do not include construction costs, architect fees, or license transfer purchase prices.
